summary: Security review completed read-only. G1 security readiness is conditional on freezing RBAC/action matrix, tenant repository contract, approval-token semantics, object-storage key policy, and agent tool-gateway enforcement requirements.
decisions: Treat browser/API, API/database/object/event, core/compute/model, external systems, and uploaded/retrieved content as explicit trust boundaries.
Enforce tenant scope server-side with company_id from authenticated context.
Freeze per-endpoint and per-tool RBAC before P2.
Approval tokens must be short-lived, single-purpose, company/actor/entity/action/idempotency bound, auditable, and checked immediately before execution.
Prompt text is not a security control; the tool gateway enforces policy.
Object storage requires generated keys, MIME/extension/size validation, scan adapter, short-lived URLs, SHA-256 metadata, and no executable rendering of untrusted HTML.
Logs and traces redact tokens, credentials, prompts, sensitive tool payloads, PII, supplier credentials, and raw external documents.
assumptions: Demo credentials are acceptable only as dev-only examples and must fail production validation if placeholders remain.

verification.command: Get-Content -Raw on security, prompt, tool, config, and orchestration files

blockers: G1 should not pass security readiness until RBAC/action matrix, tenant rules, approval-token contract, and upload/object safety rules are explicit.
residual_risks: Broad tool payload schemas may permit overposting or confused-deputy writes.
company_id in tool inputs can cause cross-tenant access if not overwritten or verified.
Optional approval_token fields must be centrally enforced.
Prompt-injection tests need expansion for tool-output injection, malicious PDFs/CSVs, filenames, and stale tool results.
Production startup must reject placeholder secrets.
requested_next_action: Freeze RBAC/tool authorization matrix, approval-token semantics, tenant repository contract, object/file safety contract, logging redaction policy, and required negative tests.
